text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - Japan's Food Agency said on Thursday it bought 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 50,000 of Canadian wheat, 20,000 of Australian wheat and 20,000 tonnes of Australian barley at its weekly tender.

SOYBEAN SALE - USDA said Thursday U.S. soybean sales to China totaled 55,000 tonnes in the week ended July 24. In its weekly export sales report, USDA said the soybeans are for delivery during the 1996/97 marketing year.

WHEAT SALE - The CCC said it bought 3,530 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for donation to Honduras. The CCC said the wheat was purchased from Cargill Inc at $148.29 a tonne, FOB. The delivery period was slated for August 15-September 5.
WHEAT TENDERS - Iraq is in the world grain market with a tender for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for August or September, European grain traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - Jordan is tendering on August 12 for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat. One shipment of 50,000 tonnes is for October delivery and the rest for November, European traders said.
- Morocco was seeking a total of 120,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat to be delivered in August and September, European traders said. Offers were due August 4.

- The CCC was seeking up to 6,500 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Armenia and 6,500 tonnes of U.S. HRW wheat for donation to Georgia. Shipment was slated for Aug 20-Sept 8. Offers are due August 5.

Armenia was also seeking 1,000 to 1,500 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better HRW wheat in bulk under the PL-480, Title I export program, its U.S. export agent said. Delivery dates were set for Aug 20-Sept 8 and offers were due Aug 5.

VEGOIL TENDERS - Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries will seek on August 19, 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes of crude sunflower and/or semi-refined cottonseed oil for delivery in the second half of September.
MARKET TALK - China is unlikely to import corn this year despite the high probability of a shrunken crop but may have to turn to imports at the end of 1998, grains traders said.

... Thailand on Thursday approved a proposal by palm oil producers to import 20,000 tonnes of crude palm oil to alleviate local shortages, a commerce ministry official said. The imports, which are likely from Malaysia or Indonesia, must be delivered by the end of August, the official said.
